title: Kahana vs Zenler: Discovery Beside the LMS
excerpt: Zenler is course creation and live-class platform aimed at coaches and online educators. Kahana is discovery + cohort discussion around teaching you already run elsewhere.

columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

scaleFacts: Built for creators, coaches, and educators who want courses, community, live classes, and marketing in one platform.

Drag-and-drop courses with multimedia (video, PDFs, audio, ebooks, PowerPoint, SCORM/HTML), quizzes, surveys, assignments, certificates, drip, live classes, community, email, funnels, affiliates, payments, analytics.
Marketing positions ~USD 97/month vs stacking tools at ~USD 660/month; unlimited courses/students and zero transaction fees, “every feature on every plan.”
Case studies cite creators generating USD 15K in month one, 300+ paying members, and up to ~USD 37K monthly revenue.

strengths.title: All-in-one teaching and marketing stack
strengths.detail: Course hosting, website, email, funnels, live classes, community, payments, and analytics under one login.

strengths.title: Unlimited courses and students, no transaction fees
strengths.detail: Predictable pricing with unlimited courses/students and zero transaction fees as you scale.

strengths.title: Rich course and assessment tools
strengths.detail: Video, audio, PDFs, SCORM/HTML, quizzes, assignments, certificates, and drip with a mobile-responsive player.

strengths.title: Fast setup with templates and one-click creation
strengths.detail: 1,000+ page templates and one-click course creation to publish courses and checkout pages quickly.

weaknesses.title: Less brand recognition than bigger LMS players
weaknesses.detail: Lower profile than Teachable, Thinkific, Kajabi, or LearnWorlds, fewer third-party resources and ecosystems.

weaknesses.title: Potentially opinionated stack
weaknesses.detail: All-in-one means adopting Zenler’s approach to sites, email, funnels, and community, may limit best-of-breed swaps.

weaknesses.title: Limited granular pricing clarity in marketing
weaknesses.detail: Heavy “savings vs stack” messaging; specific plan structures and advanced limits need deeper digging.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. Zenler is course creation and live-class platform aimed at coaches and online educators. They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

Zenler is an all-in-one online course platform for coaches, trainers, and creators that includes your course builder, website, email marketing, sales funnels, live classes, community, payments, and analytics under one login. Official site.

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and Zenler side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On Zenler you can use Courses, Memberships, and Storefronts as first-class product jobs. You are running a full course engine: drip, quizzes, student progress, and checkout that already works.

Using Kahana with Zenler

You can use both. Zenler keeps doing what it already does well. Kahana is another place to package the work, get discovered, and grow an audience.

Keep the course engine on Zenler for drip, quizzes, and enrollment. Also list or link that teaching on Kahana so Explore, Clubs, and Aura can give it another place to be found. Zenler stays the LMS; Kahana is another surface for exposure.
